financing.summary: Smith Douglas is one of the most land-light public builders: it buys finished lots just in time through lot-option contracts with third-party developers and unnamed land bankers, and at 2026-09-30 owned only 517 unstarted lots (2.1% of its 24,724 controlled lots). Land banking is an established, growing channel: land bank deposits rose from $34.2M on 3,232 lots (end 2024) to $62.8M on 5,637 lots (end 2025), and total option deposits were $142.3M against a $1.42B remaining option purchase price at 2026-09-30. Corporate funding is a single $325M unsecured Wells Fargo-agented revolver (maturity May 2029; $99.0M drawn, about $204.1M available at 2026-09-30) with no public notes and no disclosed ratings. With cash at $5.9M, revolver use up from $40M to $99M in nine months, and a first self-developed Houston community (Pinemoor, 216 lots), the company has room and reason to add off-balance-sheet lot capital in its Southeast and Texas markets; no land-bank counterparty is publicly named.
financing.land_strategy: Land-light, 'just-in-time' finished-lot model in the company's own framing: acquires finished lots through lot-option contracts with third-party developers and land bankers (deposits typically 5-20% of price, non-refundable after a 60-120 day inspection period, staggered takedowns); in land-bank deals it assigns its land or lot contracts to the land banker, which funds development and sells finished lots back over time with interest on the outstanding lot price, and the company may also agree to develop the lots at a fixed cost. Targets: about a four-year lot supply in every market, no more than about two months of owned finished lots and four months of started lots on the balance sheet; 96% of unstarted controlled lots were optioned at end 2025 and 2024. No formal percent-optioned target is stated.

lots.note: Owned 2,031 = 517 owned unstarted lots + 1,514 homes under construction. pct_optioned computed (22,693/24,724); of unstarted lots only, optioned share is about 97.8% (22,693/23,210, computed). years_supply computed as 24,724 / 2,908 FY2025 closings (Inferred arithmetic). FY2025 10-K by segment at 2025-12-31: Southeast 932 owned / 13,938 optioned / 14,870 total; Central 780 / 6,618 / 7,398; total 1,712 / 20,556 / 22,268. The 10-Q MD&A also cites $138.4M of non-refundable deposits on 15,099 lots with about $1.1B remaining purchase price at 2026-09-30 (a narrower count than the 22,693 optioned lots).

land_banking.note: Counterparties not named in 10-K or 10-Q. CEO Greg Bennett said in 2023 the company had aligned with 'a number of land bank and capital providers' and finances all land off balance sheet (HousingWire, 2023-08-01). Q3 2026 10-Q gives no updated land-bank-only lot count.
land_banking.counterparty: Unnamed land bank partners (not publicly disclosed)
land_banking.description: Company assigns land or lot contracts to land bankers, which acquire and develop the land and sell finished lots to Smith Douglas on lot-option contracts; exposure limited to deposits and land-bank fees, plus possible fixed-cost development completion obligations. Land bank deposits were $62.8M covering 5,637 lots at 2025-12-31, up from $34.2M on 3,232 lots at 2024-12-31.

land_banking.note: At 2025-12-31: $132.2M deposits, $1,269.0M remaining price; 10-K counts 20,556 option lots overall. Lot option abandonment charges 9M 2026: Southeast $4.0M, Central $1.5M.
land_banking.counterparty: Third-party lot developers (finished lot option contracts, unnamed)
land_banking.description: Finished-lot option contracts with third-party developers: total option deposits $134.4M with $1,389.1M remaining purchase price at 2026-09-30 (excluding unconsolidated entities); none consolidated as VIEs and none treated as financing arrangements. Maximum exposure to loss about $55.4M.

land_banking.note: Lot count (550) is as of 2025-12-31 from the FY2025 10-K; partners not named.
land_banking.description: Option contracts with unconsolidated entities in which the company holds non-controlling equity interests (two entities develop and sell lots): deposits $7.9M, remaining purchase price $31.2M at 2026-09-30; 10-K cites $8.3M deposits on 550 lots at 2025-12-31.

debt.note: Drawn $99.0M at 2026-09-30 (vs $40.0M at 2025-12-31); LCs $0.8M; borrowing-base availability about $204.1M. $100M accordion, $20M LC sublimit, one-year extension option. Borrowing base on land, lots under development and finished lots. Covenants: min TNW $286.1M + 32.5% of post-1Q25 pre-tax income + 50% of new equity; max leverage 60%; EBITDA/interest >= 2.0x; min liquidity $15M. Lender list and agent from Exhibit 10.1 to the 2025-05-21 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1982518/000198251825000026/sdhc-20250515xexx101.htm

Devon Street $5.0M 8% seller note fully repaid at its 2026-09-30 maturity.
Revolver borrowings rose to $99.0M from $40.0M at year-end 2025 ($59.0M net borrowings in 9M 2026) while cash fell to $5.9M; debt-to-book capitalization rose to 18.8% from 9.0%.

ma.description: Bought substantially all assets of Houston builder Devon Street Homes (324 closings in 2022, about 1,500 lots controlled), funded partly by a $5.0M 8% seller note; Smith Douglas's entry into Texas. Context only (pre-2025).
ma.map_impact: Created the Houston division (now part of the Central segment); founder Stephen Ray led it until 2024-12-31. No 2025 or 2026 M&A: growth into Dallas-Fort Worth and the Alabama Gulf Coast in 2025 was organic.
